prompt: A salesperson closes a sale on $20\%$ of her calls, independently. Let $Y$ be the number of calls she makes up to and including her first sale. What is the expected value of $Y$?
hint: $Y$ counts trials up to and including the first success. That kind of waiting-time variable has a special name and a simple mean.

hints.text: $Y$ counts trials up to and including the first success. That kind of waiting-time variable has a special name and a simple mean.
$Y$ is geometric with $p = 0.2$, and the mean of a geometric variable is $\frac{1}{p}$, so compute $\frac{1}{0.2}$.
$\frac{1}{0.2} = 5$, so she expects to make $5$ calls to get her first sale.

explanation: Each call is an independent trial and the first sale is the first success, so $Y$ is geometric with $p = 0.2$.
The mean of a geometric variable is $\mu_Y = \frac{1}{p}$, because rarer successes take longer to arrive.
$\frac{1}{0.2} = 5$, so on average her first sale comes on call number $5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rate thinking
steps: If 1 in 5 calls is a sale, then sales happen at a rate of one per 5 calls.
So the typical wait for the next sale is 5 calls.
